question: Is 'Partly Void, Mostly Stars' (alpine 5.7) the same climb as Thielsen's Northwest Arete, and are NW Arete and NE Buttress correctly discipline-filed (trad vs alpine)?
answer: Not confirmed as the same. Mountain Project's Thielsen area page and the NW Arete page (FA Jeff Thomas 1988, 5.6 PG13, 120 ft, Trad/Alpine) never mention Partly Void; the area page does not list Partly Void at all. The OpenBeta mirror lists Partly Void as 5.7 alpine/trad/top-rope, FA unknown, filed under a different sub-area, described as following the base of the summit pinnacle clockwise until cliffed out, then climbing the arete to the summit. The grade differs (5.7 vs 5.6) and the description is generic, so it may be a different pinnacle line or an alias, but no page says so. The 'original name' idea came only from a search snippet. Disciplines: MP lists both NW Arete and NE Buttress as trad on a volcano summit pinnacle; by owner rule roped rock on a peak is alpine.
recommendation: Do not merge. Keep both rows. Change NW Arete (or_h_mt_thielsen_northwest_arete) and NE Buttress (or_h_mt_thielsen_northeast_buttress_mclaughlin_memorial_route) discipline trad -> alpine. Revisit the merge only if a guidebook (Smoot/Bond) or a dated first-ascent record ties the name to the arete.
